Send an email Post the idea on Slack X Irina Nazarova Evil Martians CEO Tuesday, Nov 10 · 9:15 am “Why start a new company on Rails, and AI, today” Let's celebrate the new and ambitious companies choosing Ruby and Rails today. We'll hear their stories, learn from their wins, and find out what's missing: what we as the Ruby community need to build to help them grow into the big Ruby success stories of the future. Based on interviews with founders. Founded a Ruby startup in the last 2-3 years? Let's talk: cal.com/inazarova/feedback CEO at Evil Martians, co-founder at AnyCable, and organizer of the SF Ruby community. Based in Japantown, and supervised by an opinionated calico cat Murka. X GitHub LinkedIn Substack Download GIF X Vladimir Dementyev Evil Martians Principal Backend Engineer Tuesday, Nov 10 · 10:05 am “Ruby for AI and AI for Ruby” Author of AnyCable, TestProf and Layered Design for Ruby on Rails Applications. X Download GIF X Madison Sites Order.co Staff Software Engineer Tuesday, Nov 10 · 10:35 am “The System Nobody Understood (Including AI)” Every scaled Rails app has a stretch of backcountry nobody dares hike into: the part no one fully understands, so you patch it for years, until you can't. Ours had a critical bridge out there. The map showed it, the report said passable; I hiked in and it was all but gone. Our dashboards, our tenured engineers, and our AI were all confidently wrong. This is how we learned to trust only the ground. Madison Sites is based in Lake Tahoe and has been a professional Ruby developer for over 10 years. She believes that removing dead code is the sixth love language. When she's not building things with cool people on the internet, you can find her very much offline, hiking on or maintaining a trail. LinkedIn Download GIF X JP Camara Wealthbox Principal Engineer Tuesday, Nov 10 · 11:05 am “Multiplayer Rails: collaborative editing, no Node required” Your Rails app can be multiplayer! Last year I showed how to build real-time collaboration into Rails from scratch with Yjs. That work became yrby-rails and lexxy-realtime, which give Rails and Lexxy first-class Yjs support. Learn how to make your Rails app collaborative for humans and AI agents alike. JP Camara is a Principal Engineer at Wealthbox. He contributes to Ruby and Rails open source, including Ruby itself, Solid Queue, yrby, and lexxy-realtime, and writes about Ruby internals and concurrency at jpcamara.com. Jpcamara.com Bluesky Download GIF X Ben Sheldon Frontdoor Benefits Co-Founder and CTO Tuesday, Nov 10 · 1:15 pm “Building the same app twice: same problems, different decade” Ten years ago I helped build and scale a welfare benefits app to aid more than 1 million people a year. Now, I'm doing it all again from the beginning. I'll compare the original 2016 product roadmap to what's possible in 2026, including feature appetites, team composition and enablement, and very, very different build-vs-buy decisions for an even more monolithic product. Ben Sheldon is the author of GoodJob, an Active Job backend. A Rails developer for over 10 years, he has worked at GitHub, OkCupid Labs, and Code for America. Ben is currently co-founder and CTO of Frontdoor Benefits. LinkedIn Download GIF X Svyatoslav Kryukov Evil Martians Senior Backend Engineer Tuesday, Nov 10 · 1:45 pm “Agents Scale, Humans Don't: Hiring Without Slowing Down” One founder plus thirty agents ships more than a team of ten. Hire a second engineer and everything slows down. Why? You didn't add an engineer, you added a second team. We'll look at the fixes that fail, then at those I believe work well with Rails, and finally at what a founder must give up to get faster. Dedicated to bridging Rails and the JavaScript ecosystem. A core maintainer of Inertia Rails, and the creator of Typelizer (automatic TypeScript types from Ruby) and TurboMount (component-based widgets for Hotwire). Writes about Rails and frontend on the Evil Martians blog. X Download GIF X Carmine Paolino Chat with Work , RubyLLM Founder Tuesday, Nov 10 · 2:15 pm “RubyLLM 2.2: The AI Framework Python Should Envy” RubyLLM brought one beautiful AI API to Ruby and passed 14 million downloads. 2.2 puts agents to work: running code in sandboxes on your servers, learning workflows from skills, using MCP tools, and turning files into finished work. Durable jobs, human approvals, evaluations, tracing, and a ledger for every billable attempt. Live demos, plain Ruby, native Rails. Ruby is where you ship AI. Carmine Paolino created RubyLLM and founded Plenty, his one-person software company behind Chat with Work, Spotifast, ZapFast, and Solco, a DJ library app. He helps organize Berlin.rb and makes house and disco as Crimson Lake. Before Ruby, he spent a decade doing machine learning in Python. Paolino.me X Download GIF X CJ Avilla Anthropic Member of Technical Staff Tuesday, Nov 10 · 3:05 pm “Assign to Claude: Making an Agent a First‑Class Teammate in Your SaaS” Most AI features are a chat box bolted onto the product. The good ones are woven through it: an agent you assign a card to, that triages the ticket before you read it, that spots a bad deploy and opens the incident itself. We'll build all three live in one Rails app on Claude Managed Agents (MCP, custom tools, memory, human approvals) and leave you a map of the agent-shaped holes in your product. CJ Avilla is a Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic and former Stripe Developer Advocate. X YouTube Download GIF X Sergey Karayev Superconductor Co-founder Tuesday, Nov 10 · 3:35 pm “The Multiplayer Al Manifesto: Teamwork in the Agentic Engineering Era.” AI has made individuals faster, but teams are not seeing proportional productivity gains. One reason is that today's AI tools are fundamentally single-player. Drawing on our team's experience, we present five principles for truly multiplayer AI and offer practical guidance for building or choosing a solution. Sergey Karayev is building Superconductor, the multiplayer AI platform for your team and agents. He has been working with Ruby on Rails for over 20 years. He has a PhD in Computer Science from UC Berkeley, and previously built a successful ed tech startup. X Download GIF X Ryan Sherlock Fin (ex Intercom) Senior Director of Engineering Tuesday, Nov 10 · 4:15 pm “Who Watches the Agents? Closing the Rails Loop from Code to Customers” At Fin, over 95% of pull requests are Agent-driven and most are approved without human review. This talk follows changes through our fifteen-year-old, three-million-line Rails monolith, from automated review and selective testing to production monitoring and rollback. Safe speed comes from layers of evidence, bounded authority, and fast recovery, not one perfect reviewer. Ryan Sherlock is Senior Director of Engineering at Fin, leading infrastructure and core technologies. He works on reliability, developer productivity, and the three-million-line Rails monolith that powers Fin at scale. X LinkedIn Download GIF X Rosa Gutiérrez 37signals Principal programmer Wednesday, Nov 11 · 9:00 am “Solid Queue: two years on Rails” Solid Queue 1.0 was released in September 2024 as the default Active Job backend in Rails. 2.0 is ready, but the world is completely different now! Let's explore the path to that new version and the new features, as well as how maintaining an open-source project has changed since Solid Queue was started. Rosa has worked with Ruby for over 13 years. She loves maths, theoretical computer science, learning languages for both humans and computers, and her dog Mochi. Bluesky Download GIF X Celina Lopez Primary Health Technical Lead Wednesday, Nov 11 · 9:50 am “Building a Developer-friendly PaaS for Kubernetes on Ruby” Self taught software engineer with more than 5+ years of experience. Built software which helped vaccinate/test more than 7 million people in the US. Currently contributing to an open-source platform that simplifies application deployment using Kubernetes. GitHub Download GIF X Jason Bosco Typesense CEO & Co-Founder Wednesday, Nov 11 · 10:20 am “How We Bootstrapped an Open Source Search Engine to $10M+ ARR with 15 People and Ruby on Rails” Bootstrapped an open-source search engine on Rails. It answers 10B+ searches a month. X Download GIF X Marco Roth Herb Wednesday, Nov 11 · 10:50 am “Reactive Rails Views, No Rewrite Required” What if your existing Rails views could become reactive without rewriting them? In this talk, we'll explore how ReActionView brings fine-grained reactivity to HTML+ERB while staying compatible with Action View. We'll look at how existing templates can become reactive, how updates are tracked and rendered, and what this could mean for the future of the Rails view layer. Marco is a passionate full-stack developer and a dedicated open-source contributor. He has open-sourced, maintained, and contributed to numerous libraries in the Ruby ecosystem and was awarded the Rails Luminary Award in 2025. X Download GIF X Alex Coomans Persona Software Engineer at Persona - Infrastructure Team Wednesday, Nov 11 · 1:00 pm “Keeping Your Head on Straight in Concurrent & Complex Ruby Applications” Ruby applications depend on execution-scoped state, but Threads, Fibers, requests, and jobs can lose it, leak it, or restore it incorrectly. This talk introduces Persona’s Context abstraction for safely inheriting and overriding that state, shows how we built dynamic configuration systems on top of it, and offers patterns you can apply in your own Ruby applications. Alex is a long time Rubyist with a love for intricate and mind-boggling puzzles. At Persona, he's focused on enabling product teams by developing & maintaining robust, scalable infrastructure - ranging across Rails, Kubernetes, Cloud IaC - and everything in between. GitHub LinkedIn Download GIF X Phillip Campbell Gusto Senior Engineering Manager Wednesday, Nov 11 · 1:30 pm “Background processing at Gusto: The Parts Where People Look Puzzled” An update/extension/reformulation of my talk from Rocky Mountain Ruby www.youtube.com/watch?v=aY_yKeZYzko Phillip Campbell is an engineering leader at Gusto, where he leads the teams responsible for Rails architecture and background processing. He’s passionate about developer productivity at scale and focuses on building systems that help engineers stay fast, effective and happy in complex environments. LinkedIn Download GIF X Peter Zhu Shopify Ruby Core Committer & Staff Software Engineer Wednesday, Nov 11 · 2:00 pm “Open Source is the Most Fragile and Most Resilient Ecosystem” The open source software that powers our businesses is maintained primarily by volunteers but funded by too few companies. This talk reframes open source support as not charity, but rather a critical part of the business’ infrastructure. We will be discussing why your company needs a team to manage your open source stack, how to manage this team, and the benefits they could provide. Peter is a Ruby core committer and a Staff Software Engineer at Shopify. He works on improving the performance of Ruby and has worked on various projects including Modular GC, Ractors, and Variable Width Allocation. He is currently based in Tokyo, Japan. X Bluesky Ruby.social LinkedIn Download GIF X Cole Robertson Rebulk Wednesday, Nov 11 · 2:50 pm “Building a new startup on Rails and Starlink” YC S25. Measures bulk inventory nobody can barcode, with LiDAR and computer vision. Download GIF X Jason Thomas OpenC3 CTO Wednesday, Nov 11 · 3:20 pm “Satellite command and control with Ruby and COSMOS” COSMOS began at Ball Aerospace to scratch an itch: can I make an easy to use and configure command and control system? This talk traces that journey — from an internal tool at a big aerospace company, to open source in an industry where almost nothing is open, to OpenC3, the company we founded to steward COSMOS. Ends with how we built line-by-line Ruby script execution. Jason graduated from Iowa State University and spent 20 years at Ball Aerospace, where he was instrumental in building COSMOS. In 2022 he co-founded OpenC3 with Ryan Melton to commercialize COSMOS, where he now serves as CTO, building the next generation of COSMOS features. LinkedIn Download GIF X Chris Oliver GoRails , Hatchbox Founder Wednesday, Nov 11 · 4:00 pm “Rails: The Founder's Unfair Advantage” Chris is a Rails Luminary, entrepreneur and content creator. He makes weekly Ruby on Rails screencasts at GoRails.com, a Ruby on Rails SaaS template called Jumpstart Pro and a hosting service called Hatchbox.io.
